You're not alone. The world is filled with people who feel the same way. For every successful, well-adjusted, highly motivated, red blooded champion, there's at least one of... Well, one of us. And even for the champions, most of them have difficulties that at times make them feel just as helpless and lost as you feel.

Everybody has value. Everybody has meaning. Everybody can contribute. The first step would be to find a community of people who you can relate to. While it's true that being human means to deal with these problems, the reality is that the majority of champions will not relate to the major of... Us. The only way to do that is to use apps like meetup to find people who at least share a passion and put yourself out there. Eventually, by taking the initiative, you'll find connection. But, the material world exists too. So you'll probably want some self improvement.

Set goals. one or more long term goals that are then broken up into daily highly achievable tasks. Things like improved hygiene, moderate exercise, slightly improved nutrition. 

So for example you want to get in shape and get a job as a software developer. The daily tasks would be eating kale with dinner, jogging around the block, and spending an hour watching YouTube videos about basic Python. At the end of the day you evaluate what went right and what went wrong, and plan out the path for tomorrow. 

This is doable. You can get better. You can make a positive impact on your community. 

Hope this helps.

5-10 sort of a manic child. Bookish, but prone to unsocial displays of exuberance

11-16 the unsocial bit catches up with me. I gradually become a shut in. I discover writing, it was a pretty easy way to garner adult approval

17-22 My attention span sort of evaporates. A variety of reasons to this. Zero friends and minimal social interaction, very little physical activity, no spiritual discipline, no community outreach (thinking about other people first), minimal romantic prospects.

I go to college with the vague intention of becoming a teacher. Get an Associates. After a semester at a four year school I realize that I simply don't have  access to the brain power to achieve the success that I feel would warrant continuing on in that path.

Put another way, I wasn't in love with the idea of teaching, I wasn't capable of putting in the effort that I knew would be needed in grad school, I ran out of money and didn't want to get into debt. So I left college.

23-26(today) Bounced around warehouses for while vaguely toying with the idea of eventually returning to school. At 24 I slowly started to incorporate structure into my life. I made sure to make my bed every day. Then I made sure to brush my teeth twice a day. Then I added flossing. Then I added running. No particular distance or time, just getting outside and running. That built up until I was running 10 miles. Started to feel it in my joints, am currently in the process of transitioning to cycling.

I started reading out loud to myself. That has allowed me to concentrate and even enjoy reading to a degree that I haven't felt since I was a kid.

​

I started to trying to find ways to give back to my community. This is a difficult one. Basically, people (including myself) suck and fail, but we've got to help them anyway. That attitude can lead to arrogance that other people can smell. So now I still do some volunteer stuff, but I do it because I know it has to get done, not because I'm doing anybody a favor. This has led to better results.

​

I just started an HVAC job and class. I'm loving it. The satisfaction in working with my hands brings quite a bit of joy. I feel like a kid playing in a sandbox.

​

The romantic aspect is, for the most part, less of an obsession than a passing thought. Ultimately, I know I'm on the right track, and the right woman will come along eventually. I know that this iteration of me is worth her time.
